name: VirtIO/vsock device
description: Firecracker's emulated VirtIO-vsock device. Single-instance per microVM. Mediates between AF_UNIX sockets on the host and AF_VSOCK sockets in the guest. Bypasses vhost-vsock kernel code on the host (vhost-style I/O is implemented in the Firecracker userspace VMM, not the kernel) — but still requires vhost-vsock as a host kernel module (CONFIG_VHOST_VSOCK=m).

name: CID/port addressing
description: AF_VSOCK addresses guest endpoints by (CID, port). Reserved CIDs: 0=Hypervisor, 1=Local, 2=Host. Guest CID is configurable via PUT /vsock.guest_cid (must be ≥3). Ports are 32-bit; same conventions as TCP/UDP. Inside the guest, /dev/vsock exposes the standard Linux vsock API.

name: UDS multiplexing pattern
description: All vsock traffic for a microVM funnels through a single host-side AF_UNIX socket (the configured uds_path). Per-port channels are multiplexed: host-initiated uses an in-band 'CONNECT <port>\n' command; guest-initiated maps to per-port AF_UNIX sockets at <uds_path>_<port>. Lets one Firecracker process expose unbounded vsock channels via a single socket.

name: Host-initiated CONNECT/OK handshake
description:
Sequence: host connects to UDS at uds_path → sends 'CONNECT <port>
' (port is decimal, 
 is ASCII 0x0A) → Firecracker forwards to the guest-side listener → on success replies 'OK <hostside-port>
'. If no guest listener, Firecracker terminates the host connection.

name: Guest-initiated per-port UDS pattern
description: Sequence: guest connects to (CID=2 host, port=N) → Firecracker tries to forward to a host-side AF_UNIX socket listening at <uds_path>_<N> → if exists, channel established; if not, VIRTIO_VSOCK_OP_RST sent back to guest (connection refused). Convention: host pre-creates listeners for each port the guest is expected to call.

name: Vsock connection reset on snapshot restore
description: All open vsock connections are closed across snapshot/restore. Listening sockets in the guest survive — they accept fresh connections post-resume. Orchestrators must design control-plane protocols to tolerate this (idempotent operations + reconnect logic).

name: vsock_override on snapshot restore
description: PUT /snapshot/load supports a vsock_override.uds_path field to remap the host UDS path on restore. Critical when running multiple clones of the same snapshot in environments without the jailer (where chroots would otherwise isolate paths) — avoids UDS-path collision between simultaneous clones.
